answer: Identity weight is anchored to scarce namespace, not keys. Each agent must control a distinct DNS zone over two years old, publishing a signed TXT record re-read at random moments; call that probe a pulse. Creation dates cannot be backdated, so a farm cannot mint supply: it must buy aged domains on the aftermarket, where each identity costs real money. A quarterly yarrow sweep clusters zones by registrant, nameserver and hosting ASN, collapsing a shared cluster into one graph vertex, so a thousand clones weigh one. Cloning costs N aged domains plus forfeited deposits; honest agents pay once.
